title: Pricing + Hiring Tradeoffs: Scenario Bridge & Sensitivity Workbook
body:
Purpose:
This working workbook outlines multi-scenario tradeoffs between incremental pricing changes, hiring cadence (the "hiring bridge"), and the resulting impact on 12-month runway and net burn.

TL;DR:
- Small, phased price increases (3–7%) combined with targeted hiring pauses can materially extend runway (~3–6 months) with limited revenue churn risk under baseline elasticity assumptions.
- Conservative assumptions (higher churn/elasticity) require deeper headcount slowdowns or a larger price change to achieve the same runway extension.
- Recommend a staged approach: 1) 3% price increase for new customers + grandfathered existing customers for 90 days; 2) hiring pause for non-customer-facing roles for 1 quarter; 3) monitor net expansion and churn weekly, revert/hard-stop on early warning signals.

Key assumptions (baseline):
- ARR at start of model: $46.2M annualized (Feb 2026 run-rate).
- Monthly churn (gross) baseline: 1.6%; uplifted churn if price change >=5%: +0.9pp (conservative).
- Price elasticity: baseline -0.25 (i.e., 1% price rise -> 0.25% demand drop), conservative scenario -0.6.
- Average revenue per customer (ARPC): $3.9k / month baseline.
- Hiring ramp: baseline plan adds 26 FTEs over 4 quarters (mix: infra/eng 40%, product 25%, sales/CS 25%, g&a 10%).
- Opex per FTE fully loaded: $220k/year (salaries + benefits + tools + infra allocation).
- Non-headcount opex growth: base + 4% YoY.

Scenario definitions:
1) Baseline: No price change, full hiring plan.
2) Small lift + short pause: +3% price realized month 1 for new customers and rolled to all customers by month 3, hiring freeze for non-customer-facing hires for 1 quarter (delay 10 FTEs).
3) Medium lift + targeted slowdowns: +6% price, hiring pause for 2 quarters for non-customer-facing (delay 16 FTEs), limited hiring in CS/sales to avoid customer friction.
4) Conservative downside (stress): +3% price but elasticity high (-0.6), churn increases; require hiring cut of 20 FTEs to match runway target.

Quick sensitivity matrix (illustrative):
- Price change vs. net ARR change (12-month run):
  - +0% price -> ARR change 0%
  - +3% price (baseline elasticity -0.25) -> ARR net +2.25% (gross revenue up 3.0% minus 0.75% demand loss)
  - +6% price -> ARR net +4.8% (gross 6.0% - demand loss 1.2%)
  - +3% price (stress elasticity -0.6) -> ARR net +1.2% (gross 3.0% - demand loss 1.8%)

Simplified 12-month P&L delta per scenario (high level, $k):
Columns: Scenario | Revenue delta | Opex delta (headcount) | Net delta | Runway effect (months)
- Baseline | +0 | +5,720 | -5,720 | 0
- Small lift + short pause | +1,041 | +4,300 | -3,259 | +2.8
- Medium lift + targeted slowdowns | +2,226 | +3,820 | -1,594 | +4.5
- Conservative downside | +554 | +4,920 | -4,366 | +1.1

Notes on the table above: revenue delta is modeled off ARR and elasticity assumptions; opex delta accounts for delayed hires (reduced run-rate) and standard non-HR spend. Runway effect is computed by dividing cash-on-hand buffer by monthly net burn delta (illustrative).

Hiring bridge (detailed plan):
ASCII table showing planned hires vs delayed hires by function (counts):
Planned hires (next 4 quarters) -- function / planned / delay-option A / delay-option B
- Eng (infra/runtime) / 10 / 4 / 6
- Product / 6 / 2 / 4
- Sales/CS / 6 / 0 / 1
- G&A / 4 / 4 / 4
Total / 26 / 10 / 15

Rationale: prefer to protect customer-facing hiring in all scenarios. Delay engineering hires that are longer-term (platform, infra optimizations) where short-term deferral has less visible customer impact. G&A hires can be paused with minimal revenue effect but have employee morale considerations if prolonged.

Early warning metrics and gating logic (to move from stage -> revert):
- Weekly: net expansion MRR (accounts with increased spend) > -1% week-over-week? If below, pause next price cohort; if below -3% for 2 consecutive weeks, rollback.
- Churn: monthly gross churn > 2.5% -> immediately halt price rollout and re-open hiring.
- Support volume and NPS: 30-day rolling spike in new support tickets per account > 25% -> review pricing messaging/or reverse.

Unit economics spot-checks (monthly):
- LTV/CAC baseline: 12.1x; 3% price lift improves LTV by ~2.2% (assuming baseline elasticity).
- Payback period baseline: 9.8 months; with hiring pauses, payback shortens as CAC investments are reduced.

Action recommendations (near term):
1) Run a small, controlled +3% price cohort for new signups by March 1; measure conversion and early churn out to 60d.
2) Implement 6-week hiring freeze on non-customer-facing reqs starting March 8; immediate HR runbook to communicate timeline and criteria.
3) Finance to instrument weekly dashboard: ARR, cohort churn, net expansion, support volume, FTE run-rate. Shared Slack channel + automated Confluence updates.
4) Legal and Product to finalize messaging and T&Cs for grandfathering period (90 days).

Open questions / items to model deeper:
- More granular customer segmentation: price sensitivity likely varies by ARR bucket and industry. A per-cohort elasticity matrix would change the recommended rollouts.
- Impact on enterprise renewals already in a >60-day sales window; need sales ops input on timing sensitivity.
- Potential to pair price increase with packaging changes (e.g., enforce minimum commit tiers) to reduce churn risk.

Appendix: scenario inputs (compact):
- Cash on hand: $124.5M
- Monthly burn (baseline): $5.3M
- Target runway extension: 3 months without raising funds
- Hiring deferral options mapped to calendar quarters and cost savings per deferred FTE: $18k–$40k per deferred quarter (depends on role and ramp profile).

If helpful I can extract the model into a shared sheet and create a per-customer-segment sensitivity tab. Next steps: confirm cohort rules for the +3% pilot and finalize hiring freeze communications by EOD Friday.

Document owner: Asha Patel (finance); please ping on Slack #finance-pricing for live edits.
